props.gloss_en: a person may wrap himself in a canopy and its straps and go out to the public domain on Shabbat, without concern
one who goes out on Shabbat in a garment that is not fringed as required is liable a sin-offering
tzitzit, relative to a garment, are significant and are not nullified
these [the canopy's straps] are not significant and are nullified
a person may use artifice with a strainer on Yom Tov -- [suspending it] to hang pomegranates in it -- and [then] hang sediment in it
and that is when he [actually] hung pomegranates in it
one may brew beer on the moed for the needs of the moed
not for the needs of the moed -- forbidden, date beer and barley beer alike
even though they have old [beer], one uses artifice and drinks from the new
there [the beer] the matter is not evident
here [the strainer] the matter is evident
[the young scholar] took a garlic slice and put it in the barrel's spout, and said: I intend to store it
and he went and slept in a ferry, crossed to the other side and inspected his fruit, and said: I intend to sleep
[this] artifice is in a rabbinic matter
and a young scholar will not come to do it ab initio

objections.gloss_en: מאי שנא מדרב הונא -- an unfringed garment's fringes make one liable for carrying, so why are the canopy's straps permitted? (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest, rule 12)

objections.gloss_en: מאי שנא מהא דתניא ... מערים ושותה מן החדש -- the beer artifice needs no demonstrated permitted use, so why must he actually hang pomegranates?
